extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers (PIs, postdocs, faculty, research administrators) seeking NIH and private foundation grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: Resources and consulting aimed at teaching biomedical researchers how to write competitive NIH and private-foundation grant applications, including live bootcamps, self-paced courses, and manuscript-style editing/advising. Emphasizes practical grantsmanship skills that transfer across submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling application that engages and convinces reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a compelling grant application that engages and convinces reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site repeatedly frames success as producing applications that 'engage and convince reviewers.' Testimonials describe improved scores and funding outcomes (R01, R37, K awards) after making proposals more convincing. Emphasis is on writing and presentation that persuades reviewers of importance and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address all critical points in the FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all critical points in the FOA (funding opportunity announcement) are hit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients report that 'She ensured that all critical points in the foa were hit.' Guidance implies mapping the proposal to FOA requirements and reviewer expectations is essential; missing FOA elements can prevent funding even if science is strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and readability for the general science audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the grant readable for the general science audience that will be reviewing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonials credit improved readability with successful outcomes. Advice includes simplifying presentation so non-specialist members of a study section can follow significance, approach, and innovation. Readability is tied to reviewer comprehension and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging, presentation, and formatting matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging and presentation (including formatting) significantly affect clarity and reviewer perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients report that 'Even simple things like changing the formatting made a huge difference in clarity' and reviewers compliment 'packaging and presentation.' Practical implication: formatting, layout, headings, and visual organization are part of the evaluation and can change reviewer reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured feedback to strengthen scientific content and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured, expert feedback to improve the scientific content and make the presentation clearer and more engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonial: 'Her guidance and structured feedback not only strengthened the scientific content of my proposal but also made the presentation clearer and more engaging.' Guidance implies iterative review, targeted edits, and higher-level critique (not just copyediting) improve fundability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop transferable grantsmanship skills (improve across submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training should improve clients' grantwriting skills on all submissions going forward, not only a single application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes strategic investment: members gain skills to mentor trainees, scale training at institutions, and apply techniques to future proposals (examples: trainees securing F31s). Criterion favors teaching repeatable methods and processes that increase long-term competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand NIH processes and study sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Possess knowledge of NIH study sections and internal NIH processes to inform proposal strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'Her knowledge of study sections and NIH gives our faculty a leg up in developing competitive NIH grant proposals.' Practical guidance: tailor aims, significance, and approach to likely study section makeup and scoring conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and write for reviewer thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate how reviewers think and craft proposals to answer likely reviewer concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients note the trainer 'knows how the reviewers think.' This implies teaching how to predict reviewer critiques, preempt concerns in the approach/limitations sections, and frame innovation/significance to align with reviewer priorities.
